newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore rulers back in power before election.
newsitem.headline: Singapore rulers back in power before election.

text.p: Singapore's ruling People's Action Party (PAP) has swept back to power before elections with opposition parties failing to contest a majority of seats in the 83-member parliament, government sources said on Monday.
A senior government official, who asked not to be identified, told reporters shortly after nominations closed that opposition parties would put up 36 candidates, giving the PAP 47 uncontested seats.
A senior party official also said the PAP had won 47 seats by a walkover.
Prime Minister Goh Chok Tong was due to announce a date for the election later in the day. Most analysts expect a poll date in early January.

The PAP has won every Singapore election since 1959 and before the parliament was dissolved earlier this month, the opposition held only four of the 81 seats. Redrawn constituency boundaries have added another two seats.
The failure of the opposition parties to nominate enough candidates to challenge the PAP's grip on power had been widely expected and politicians and analysts said Goh's party was never under threat.

Opposition parties say they have difficulty attracting candidates, accusing the the PAP of making life difficult for them and Goh admitted last Friday the party did not want a strong opposition voice in parliament.
He told university students that Singapore could not have made the transition to the prosperous, modern state it was now if past PAP governments had been restrained by a strong opposition.

Government ministers have also been touring constituencies over the past few days and telling voters bluntly that they could not expect lavish government renovation and development projects if they sent an opposition politician to parliament.
Goh was the bluntest, telling voters on Sunday he would respect their choice if they elect someone from the opposition.
But, he added: "Then you'll be left behind. Then in 20, 30 years' time, the whole of Singapore will be bustling away and your estate, through your own choice, will be left behind," he said.
